opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code is within policy (write allowed for full-time employees; Engineer owns Source Code). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 (Dominic Taylor) as a contractor with basic security training, which differs from the earlier note's full_time entry. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits to read; requested write exceeds policy, so recommend read.
reason: Dominic Taylor (E004) requested write access to Source Code. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full_time, but the Security agent's looked-up database shows contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; with basic training the maximum is read. Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, grant the maximum: read.
